title: The 2003 blackout grew behind a silenced alarm
body: During the Northeast blackout affecting about 55 million people, a race condition in FirstEnergy's energy-management software stalled its alarm system, so operators never saw lines failing and could not shed load in time. Trees and heat started the cascade; invisible alarms removed the humans from the loop. Monitoring that fails silently is worse than none, because it manufactures calm.
source_hint: US-Canada Power System Outage Task Force report (2004)
